posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
These subjects are taught. They belong to different parts of the śāstra.

1. Retrogression. A vakra graha is close to the Earth and bright, and its ceṣṭā bala rises. Retrogression does not change dignity in the astronomical sense: the graha stays in the rāśi it occupies. Its behaviour reverses, though. A debilitated retrograde graha behaves like an exalted one, and an exalted retrograde graha behaves like a debilitated one. A retrograde graha also carries a sense of lack, both in itself and in the houses it aspects. The theme of repetition runs through those points: matters come back, are revisited and are done again.

2. A retrograde AmK, DK and so on. The chara kārakas belong to the Jaimini model. Retrogression does not change their order. The only special case is Rāhu, whose degrees are counted backward from 30°. In Pārāśarī reading, functional nature and dignity decide what a graha gives. The Jaimini kārakas work on natural qualities.

3. Country charts. Mundane Jyotiṣa reads nations from the Sarvatobhadra Cakra, the Kūrma Cakra and the Saṅghaṭṭa Cakras. There are many more cakras besides these. It also reads the full Moon and new Moon charts and the daśās of foundation charts. The slow cycles of the outer planets add the long movements.

4. Continents and regions. The Bṛhat Saṃhitā's Kūrma Vibhāga and other texts assign the nakṣatras to directions and lands. An afflicted nakṣatra points to the land it rules.

5. Devas, asuras and humans. These are for spiritual discussions. In mundane work, we do weigh the deva, manuṣya and rākṣasa gaṇas of the populations in different parts of the world.
posts.my_take: This is the kind of breakdown I wish more people would teach. Retrogression as strength, plus that sense of lack and repetition, actually makes more sense than treating vakra as automatic doom.

I will simplify it for you. 

The effect of combustion depends on Sūrya's functional nature in the chart.

When Sūrya is a functional benefic, combustion is not bad. Sūrya lends the combust graha strength and takes over its role. Exception: Maṅgala or Śukra as 6th or 11th lord still behave badly when combust, even under a benefic Sūrya. If they are also in bad dignity, they become terrible.

When Sūrya is a functional malefic, combustion is very bad.
As a rule, a combust graha always has some of its natural significations compromised.

Jaimini's own rule is eight cara kārakas, with Rāhu included. Sūtra 1.1.10 offers seven or eight, and 1.1.18 says that "some" merge the mother and the son. 

A trikoṇa lord that becomes the GK remains a functional benefic for the houses it rules. Jaimini says "siddham anyat" (2.4.37): what he leaves unstated is settled from other works, so the Pārāśarī rules of lordship apply alongside his kārakas. Lordship and kārakatva are separate considerations and do not cancel each other; also, mixing systems will do a lot of damage. As GK, the graha adds the significations of kinsmen, rivals, obstacles and disease, and as a functional benefic it tends to give the favourable side of these matters.

quoted_post.author: VEDANJANAM
quoted_post.text:
1. True nodes or mean nodes? - Mean nodes. True node wobbles with short-period perturbations that only add noise, not meaning.

2. Lahiri, Raman, KP, Fagan-Bradley or Puṣya-pakṣa? - Lahiri. I personally use Lahiri plus 6′, on the mean equinox. Its zero point is the coincidence of the true equinox with the Meṣa saṅkrānti, and the observations of the ancients, Varahamihiri, Timocharis and Hipparchus, corroborate it. The sidereal zero point should not wobble with nutation.

3. Does a bādhaka graha become benefic if debilitated? -  No. Bādhakādhipati rules come from the Jātaka Pārijāta and later texts, not the earlier Pārāśarī texts, so they have no place in the method. Debility does not reform a graha either: a weak functional malefic becomes extremely bad.

4. Is Guru in Śravaṇa debilitated if Śani aspects it, or is there nīcabhaṅga? - Guru is debilitated. Śravaṇa lies wholly in Makara, Guru's sign of debility. There is no nīcabhaṅga. Please read my detailed post on this topic written a few days back. Śani's aspect does not lift the debility. As the aspect of Guru's dispositor, it controls Guru's results according to Śani's functional nature for that lagna. Judge Guru's final strength by its overall ṣaḍbala, since debility is only one part of sthāna bala.

posts.my_take: Mean nodes and Lahiri plus 6′ is a clear stance, and the bādhaka point is useful: later-text rules don't belong in this method. Also noted that a weak functional malefic gets worse, not better.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
A weak functional malefic does more harm, not less. Weakness does not take away its energy. It takes away its control, so the graha acts without restraint, and its bad results come out at their worst.

Nor does a weak functional benefic simply lose its power to do good. It behaves "with gay abandon": it still gives, but without measure or judgment, and its gifts come in excess or at the wrong time.

A strong graha is the reverse. A strong functional benefic behaves very well, and a strong functional malefic behaves slightly better.

Two cautions:

– Judge weakness by overall ṣaḍbala, not by one marker. 
– A sandhi is a separate matter, because it concerns the house, not the graha's nature. A graha delivers a bhāva's results fully at the madhya and only about a quarter at the ārambha and the anta. A malefic at a sandhi gives less of that bhāva's matters. Its own nature and its aspects stay fully at work, and its aspects decide the result.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
It would be presumptuous to claim to know the future by one's own power. The case here is different though.

A meteorologist reads the pressure systems, and a physician reads the pulse. Each uses an inherited body of knowledge to say what is likely to come. No one calls that presumption.

In Jyotiṣa the grahas are karmaphala-pradātās: they dispense the fruits of past karma. They do not create a destiny; they deliver one already earned.

The astrologer does not decree that harvest. He reads the season in which it ripens. That is why Jyotiṣa is called the eye of the Veda: it only sees, it does not create.

The knowledge itself is received. The rishis gave it out of grace and lobe, and the practitioner's task is to read it faithfully and humbly.

What lies beyond karma, the grace of Īśvara, no chart can bind. A humble astrologer says what the chart shows and leaves the rest.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Navāṃśa lagna vs kārakāṃśa

Both are division positions, not charts. The navāṃśa lagna is the navāṃśa of the lagna degree. It refines the lagna and shows the body, the constitution and how the self actually appears in the world. 

The kārakāṃśa (Jaimini's svāṃśa) is the navāṃśa of the ātmakāraka. From it Jaimini reads the soul's direction and its dharma, and from the 12th from it, the iṣṭa-devatā. 

Argalā vs aspect

Argalā means a bolt. It works by position, not by sight. Grahas in the 2nd, 4th and 11th from a sign, and malefics in the 3rd, hold argalā on it (Jaimini 1.1.5–1.1.6). Grahas in the 12th, 10th and 3rd respectively obstruct it, and if the obstruction is stronger, the argalā fails.

Dṛṣṭi decides what a graha does to a house. Argalā decides whether the graha gets its hand on the matter at all. The two are independent. 

A graha can aspect without holding argalā, or hold argalā without aspecting. When one graha both aspects a house and holds unobstructed argalā on it, its control is complete. 

Aspect still gives the primary result, and argalā tells you whether that intervention gets through or is blocked. With natural benefics the intervention is supportive (śubhārgalā). With natural malefics it is harmful (pāpārgalā).

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Lord or occupant: which one is causing the problem?

Look first at what controls the house. The order is aspect, then placement, then lordship. If an aspecting graha controls the house, trace its aspect chain back to the head, because the problem starts there.

Then read the signature of the problem:

An occupant's problem carries that graha's own nature and kārakatva: its shape, colour, quality and the kind of event it produces. A Maṅgala in the 4th troubles the home with fire, quarrels and cuts.

A lord's problem carries the themes of the other house the lord owns and of the house it sits in. It brings those matters into the house it rules. A 4th lord who is also the 11th lord, sitting in the 8th, troubles the home through gains, elder siblings or desires, and through sudden loss.

Daśā settles the question. The problem shows up in the daśā or antardaśā of the graha responsible for it.

Sign, graha and house lord: who is fixed and who adjusts?

- The sign is fixed. It is the field, and it sets the terms. 
- A graha adjusts to the sign it occupies, and that is what dignity means: the same graha is strong in one sign and weak in another. 
- The house lord is the house's agent. It carries the house wherever it goes and takes on the conditions of its own placement, dignity and aspects. 

So the sign is the field, the graha is the actor who must adapt to it, and the lord is the house's representative, whose condition becomes the house's condition.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Under Parāśara's rule, Mīna is not an enemy sign for Śukra, and Makara is not one for Maṅgala. Guru is neutral to Śukra, and Śani is neutral to Maṅgala. 

Parāśara counts as friends the lords of the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th and 12th from a graha's mūlatrikoṇa, along with the lord of its exaltation sign. The other lords are enemies, and a graha that falls in both lists is neutral.

From Tulā, Guru owns the 3rd and the 6th and would be Śukra's enemy. From Meṣa, Śani owns the 10th and the 11th and would be Maṅgala's. In each case, lordship of the exaltation sign lifts him to neutral.

These are the only two such cases among the seven grahas. For every other graha, the exaltation lord is a friend anyway. So exaltation is an input to the friendship table, not a result of it, and asking why a graha exalts in an enemy's sign gets the order backwards.

Exaltation is where a graha's own nature reaches its fullest and finest expression. 

Makara is the 10th of the kālapuruṣa, the seat of karma, and the 10th is where Maṅgala gains digbala. Raw force does its best work under Śani's discipline. 

Mīna is the natural 12th, the bed and mokṣa, and Śukra is classically good in the 12th. In Guru's sign the two ācāryas meet, and Śukra's rasa dissolves into devotion. He falls in Kanyā, where analysis separates what he would unite.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Judge everything from the lagna, not from the Moon sign. Candra matters as a graha, read by where it sits and what it aspects from the lagna. The Moon sign is not a second ascendant.

The hierarchy follows the rule for every house: aspect first, then placement, then lordship.

1. Grahas aspecting the lagna: They control the personality and give the main traits. A one-way aspect is especially strong. If the aspecting graha is itself under another graha's aspect, trace the chain back to its head. The head shapes the character, and each graha in the chain colours it.
2. Grahas placed in the lagna: They act on the person directly. Weigh them by position: strongest near the bhāva madhya, about a quarter strength near the ārambha or the anta.
3. The lagna lord. It carries the self wherever it goes. Its sign gives its dignity, its house shows where the person puts himself, and the aspects on it shape how he expresses himself. A conjunct graha only modifies it, and the lagna lord modifies that graha in return. Sambandha never overrides aspect.
4. The lagna sign. This is the field. It sets the native's basic temperament, which the grahas above then work on.

Two rules decide what each graha contributes:

1. Polarity. Every graha has a good face and a bad one. Functional nature and strength decide which shows. A strong, functionally benefic Guru aspecting the lagna gives wisdom. A weak or functionally malefic Guru gives arrogance and a person who listens to no one.

2. Strength. Judge it by overall ṣaḍbala, not by exaltation and debility alone.

For finer distinctions, read the lagna degree's division positions: its nakṣatra pāda, read through its navāṃśa lord, and its ṣaṣṭyaṃśa. Some traits also need their own house. Strong-headedness, for example, is read from the 3rd as well as the lagna, and the lagna is never ignored for any trait reading.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
1) Does the lagna have the main role in predicting profession?

Yes. Every prediction starts from the lagna, never from the Moon sign. The lagna sets each graha's functional nature, so the same Śani builds one career and wrecks another. The career houses are counted from it: the 10th is the work, and the 4th, 5th and 9th are the education and field that feed it. And the lagna is the person who must carry the work. A strong 10th with a weak lagna gives a position the native cannot hold on to. Read the 10th by aspect, placement, and lordship, and time it by daśā and transit. The D1 is enough.

2) Nodes in a kendra with a trikoṇa lord and a 3rd, 6th or 11th lord, dispositor in the 2nd or 12th

A node in a kendra in sambandha with a trikoṇa lord becomes a rāja yogakāraka. Only the 8th or 11th lord in that conjunction breaks the yoga. A 3rd or 6th lord does not: the yoga stands, it just becomes weaker. Then judge strength and aspects. A debilitated node (Rāhu in Vṛścika, Ketu in Vṛṣabha) delivers the yoga by any means, right or wrong. Its aspects on the 5th, 7th and 9th, and the aspects it receives, decide how the yoga shows.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
No. Retrogression is a strength, not a doom. A retrograde graha is at its nearest to the Earth and gets full cheṣṭā bala, so it is strong in ṣaḍbala. What retrogression changes is how that strength behaves.

Two rules cover it:

1. Dignity reverses in behaviour. Retrogression does not change a graha's dignity astronomically, but a debilitated graha in retrogression behaves as if exalted, and an exalted one behaves as if debilitated. Every other sign keeps its normal dignity.
2. It brings a sense of lack and repetition. The graha feels something missing in itself and in the houses it aspects, and those matters keep coming back. This is neither a permanent defect nor a struggle that ends once overcome. It is a pattern of return: the matter is revisited, redone or repeated until it settles.

Functional benefics and malefics: First find the graha's effective dignity, then use the usual strength rule.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
The Sarvatobhadra Cakra became the standard because it is complete. One 9×9 grid holds the 28 nakṣatras with Abhijit, the 12 rāśis, the letters of the alphabet, the five tithi groups and the seven weekdays.

Vedha is the single mechanism that connects them. A graha in a cell pierces along fixed lines, the front and the two diagonals, so its effect on a person, a city, a ruler or a date is read by one rule.

The same figure therefore serves natal work, praśna, muhūrta, medinī and war. Narapati, the great jyotiṣī, treats it as the master figure in his Narapatijayacaryā.

The nuance is that the SBC does not replace the other cakras. It is the general instrument, and they are specialists. The Kūrma Cakra maps the nakṣatras onto the regions of the land, the Saṅghaṭṭa Cakras read the collisions of grahas in mundane events, and the Śatapada Cakra gives letters for names. That is why the Rāśi and Nakṣatra Saṅghaṭṭa Cakras are still drawn and read on their own before their common findings are weighed.

These cakras share a form with the Śrīcakra but not a purpose. The Śrīcakra and other devatā cakras are yantras: each is the seat and body of a devatā, worshipped in upāsanā. The jyotiṣa cakras are cakras of reckoning, with no devatā installed in them. Both rest on the maṇḍala idea of ordered space with a centre and four directions.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
A nakṣatra does not decide whether a result comes or how much of it. That rests on the strength of the house and its lord. 

The nakṣatra decides the manner. 

- Its deity colours the result: Pitṛdeva in Maghā brings it through the ancestors' blessings, and a Rākṣasa in Mūla brings boundless power to act.
- Its lord sets how the native acts to win it, with service and renunciation in Ketu's nakṣatras and with imagination and joy in Śukra's. 
- The sign and its lord set the terms, the nāḍī sets the aftertaste (dahana leaves worry in the heart), and the tāra bala and the nakṣatra-bindus from Sūrya and Candra show whether the nakṣatra supports or strains the native. So one lord gives three different results in its three nakṣatras.

A nakṣatra influences the native in two ways. A house lord sitting in it brings that house's results in its manner, and a graha striking it by vedha by SBC colours the house that holds it, in the daśā and transit that trigger it.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
In Pārāśarī Jyotiṣa, a graha's natural quality (saumya or krūra) plays no part in the results. Every graha carries both good and bad kārakatvas. Functional nature decides which polarity shows, and strength decides how far it goes.

For a Tulā lagna, Guru rules the 3rd and the 6th, so he is a functional malefic and gives his negative polarity. That means extreme arrogance, a native who listens to no one, misplaced faith, excess, and false teachers, together with the 6th-house matters of enemies, debts and disease. He is not a "good graha doing harm gently". He is Guru's own bad face. Śani rules the 4th and the 5th, so he is the yogakāraka and gives his positive polarity: discipline, justice, endurance, service, detachment and lasting structure, delivered through property, learning and children. He is not a cruel graha doing good by hardship. He is Śani's own good face.

Strength sets the degree. A strong functional malefic behaves slightly better, and a weak one becomes extremely bad. A strong functional benefic behaves very well, and a weak one gives with gay abandon.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Vairāgya, inner detachment, is common in charts. Saṃnyāsa, formal renunciation, is rare. Varāhamihira's pravrajyā yoga (Bṛhajjātaka 15) needs four or more strong grahas in one sign, and the strongest of them names the order: Sūrya the forest ascetic living on wild food, Candra the aged ascetic, Maṅgala the Śākya, Budha the Ājīvika, Guru the bhikṣu, Śukra the wandering caraka, Śani the nirgrantha. If that graha is combust or defeated in graha-yuddha, the native is initiated or turns devotee but does not complete the renunciation, which comes in that graha's daśā.

From the lagna, a strong Śani or Ketu aspecting the lagna or its lord builds detachment into the character. The 12th lord in sambandha with the lagna or the 9th, or a strong Guru aspecting the 12th, turns it toward mokṣa rather than loss. A weak Śukra with an obstructed 4th and 7th leaves little to hold the native back, and Ketu in Mīna, in Vṛścika or controlling the 12th deepens it. These factors alone give a detached householder. Formal saṃnyāsa needs the classical yoga, or these factors at full strength, triggered by daśā.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Count every house from the lagna, never from Śani. 

The 10th is the field: its sign gives the nature of the work, and grahas aspecting it control the results, a functional benefic lifting the career and a functional malefic damaging it through its negative polarity. 

A graha placed in the 10th is the actor, shaping the kind of work through its kārakatvas: Sūrya authority and government, Budha trade and writing, Maṅgala engineering, police or surgery. It gives full results at the madhya and a quarter near the edges. 

The 10th lord carries the career where it sits, business or partnership from the 7th and foreign or institutional work from the 12th. Its strength is the native's staying power, and its daśā brings the turning points. 

Śani, the kāraka, shows labour, service and discipline in general, and his functional nature and strength decide whether the native works steadily or struggles. Weigh them in that order: aspect, placement, lord, then kāraka. 

Time the career by the daśās of the grahas controlling the 10th, traced back along their aspect chains, then by transit. Read the education behind it from the madhyas of the 4th, 5th and 9th.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Science has found no physical mechanism by which the planets act on us. Their gravity at the Earth is negligible: the attending doctor pulls on a newborn harder than Maṅgala does. Controlled tests, such as Carlson's double-blind study in Nature (1985), found no effect.

Jyotiṣa claims no physical mechanism. The grahas are karmaphala-pradātās, devatulya powers who dispense the fruits of the native's own karma. They indicate; they do not push. Rāhu, Ketu, the upagrahas and the lagna prove the point: they are massless, lightless mathematical points, yet they act as surely as Śani or Guru. 

The sky is a map of time against which karma ripens and can be read, which is why Jyotiṣa is called the eye of the Veda. An eye sees; it does not cause. Its test is whether its predictions come true, not whether it can name a force.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
An 8th lord is a functional malefic unless it also rules the lagna or a stronger trikoṇa, and Sūrya and Candra carry no 8th-lordship blemish. Exaltation sets only the degree: a strong functional benefic behaves very well, a strong functional malefic slightly better. It gives force to the 8th house's matters (longevity, research, the occult, inheritance and the spouse's wealth, insurance, sudden events, hidden or chronic matters) and carries them into the house it occupies. Its 7th aspect always falls on its debilitation sign, so the opposite house receives a nīca dṛṣṭi and pays the cost. Judge strength by ṣaḍbala. Dignity comes from the rāśi cakra and the house from the Chalit, where the lord gives full results at the madhya and a quarter at the edges, so an exalted lord at a bhāva edge has dignity but delivers little.

Meṣa: Maṅgala, also lagna lord, exalts in the 10th with digbala, giving a powerful career in crisis work, surgery, defence, research or insurance and strong longevity, while its nīca aspect costs the 4th, home and mother.

Vṛṣabha: Guru, a strong malefic as 8th and 11th lord, exalts in the 3rd, giving research, writing and self-made sudden gains with Guru's arrogance, while father, gurus and fortune in the 9th suffer.

Mithuna: Śani, with 9th lordship prevailing, exalts in the 5th, giving deep learning, the occult, inheritance through the father's line and long life, at the cost of gains and elder siblings.

Karka: Śani, malefic and māraka as 7th and 8th lord, exalts in the 4th without digbala, giving lasting property through inheritance or the spouse and worry over the mother's longevity, with falls in status in the 10th.

Siṃha: Guru, benefic by the 5th, exalts in the 12th in Sarala yoga, giving foreign lands, spiritual research, hospitals, āśramas and spending on dharma, while service, debts and illness in the 6th are poorly handled. Co-lord Ketu exalts in the 4th, bringing sudden turns at home with better moral conduct.

Kanyā: Maṅgala, malefic as 3rd and 8th lord, exalts in the 5th, giving technical learning, surgery and speculative swings with strain around children, at the cost of the 11th.

Tulā: Śukra, also lagna lord, exalts in the 6th in Sarala yoga, giving victory through charm and work in healing or service but health risks from indulgence, at the cost of bed pleasures and expenses.

Vṛścika: Budha, a strong malefic as 8th and 11th lord, exalts in his own sign in the 11th, giving windfalls from research, trade, speculation or insurance that come with scandal, while children and judgment in the 5th suffer.

Dhanu: Candra, free of blemish, exalts in the 6th in Sarala yoga, giving a mind strong in service, healing and competition, at the cost of sleep and emotional losses in the 12th.

Makara: Sūrya, free of blemish, exalts in the 4th without digbala, giving property and authority at home through the father or the state, with clashes with superiors in the 10th.

Kumbha: Budha, with the 8th as his mūlatrikoṇa prevailing, exalts in the 8th itself in Sarala yoga, giving long life, research, the occult, insurance and a secretive intellect, at the cost of speech, family and savings. Co-lord Rāhu exalts in the 4th.

Mīna: Śukra, malefic as 3rd and 8th lord, exalts in the lagna, giving charm, artistry, sensuality and an occult bent with sudden or chronic health episodes, while the spouse and partnerships pay.
Aspects by degree and orb decide the final result, and the lord's daśā times it.
